segs.text: Section fourteen. Thiopurine methyltransferase, T P M T, and the thiopurines. The two thiopurines are azathioprine and mercaptopurine. Azathioprine is an immunosuppressant and a prodrug; the body converts it to six mercaptopurine. Mercaptopurine itself is given for cancer, because its kinetics suit that use. Low T P M T activity changes how much of either drug becomes active.

Six mercaptopurine has competing routes. Xanthine oxidase and T P M T turn it into inactive products. Another pathway makes the active six thioguanine nucleotides, which stop cancer cells dividing but also suppress the bone marrow. So T P M T normally shunts part of the drug away from the active metabolite.

When T P M T activity is low, more drug becomes six thioguanine nucleotides, and the extra active metabolite suppresses blood cells. Low T P M T does not make the drug fail; it raises toxicity. A poor metabolizer on a standard dose risks severe immunosuppression and must get much less drug.

Two snips, single nucleotide polymorphisms, account for over ninety percent of inactivating alleles. In Caucasians the common variant is T P M T star three A, two nonsynonymous snips. In East Asians it is star three C, one snip. Both are inactivating, not gain of function. The phenotypes are extensive, intermediate and poor, measured as enzyme activity in red blood cells.
